subQuestions.questionText: The phase of meiosis during which homologous chromosomes pair up to form bivalents:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C — Prophase I (2 marks)
Homologous chromosomes pair up to form bivalents (synapsis) during Prophase I of meiosis, allowing crossing over to occur.

subQuestions.questionText: The number of chromosomes found in a normal human gamete:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C — 23 (2 marks)
A normal human gamete (sperm or ovum) is haploid (n) and contains 23 chromosomes, half the somatic cell number of 46.

subQuestions.questionText: Which structure of the eye contains the highest concentration of cone cells?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C — Yellow spot (fovea) (2 marks)
The fovea (yellow spot) on the retina has the highest concentration of cone cells and is responsible for sharp, colour vision in bright light.

subQuestions.questionText: Which of the following is the main function of FSH in females?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B — Stimulates the development of a Graafian follicle (2 marks)
Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) from the anterior pituitary stimulates the development and maturation of the Graafian follicle in the ovary.

options.B: Stimulates the development of a Graafian follicle

subQuestions.questionText: Anti-diuretic hormone (ADH) is secreted from the:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B — Posterior pituitary gland (2 marks)
ADH is produced by the hypothalamus but stored and released into the bloodstream by the posterior pituitary gland.

subQuestions.questionText: A motor neuron carries impulses:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C — From the central nervous system to an effector (2 marks)
Motor (efferent) neurons carry impulses from the CNS (brain or spinal cord) to effectors such as muscles or glands.

options.A: From a receptor to the central nervous system
options.B: Within the central nervous system only
options.C: From the central nervous system to an effector

subQuestions.questionText: When a shoot is exposed to unidirectional light, auxins:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B — Move towards the shaded side, causing cells there to elongate more (2 marks)
Auxins migrate from the lit side to the shaded side of the shoot. The higher auxin concentration on the shaded side causes greater cell elongation, bending the shoot toward the light (positive phototropism).

options.A: Move towards the lit side, causing cells there to elongate more
options.B: Move towards the shaded side, causing cells there to elongate more
options.C: Are destroyed by light, stopping all growth on the lit side
options.D: Have no effect on cell elongation

subQuestions.questionText: The corpus luteum mainly secretes:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C — Progesterone (2 marks)
The corpus luteum (formed from the ruptured Graafian follicle after ovulation) mainly secretes progesterone, which maintains the endometrium during the luteal phase.

subQuestions.questionText: When the eye focuses on a NEAR object, the ciliary muscles:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B — Contract and the suspensory ligaments slacken so the lens becomes more convex (2 marks)
For near vision (accommodation), ciliary muscles contract, suspensory ligaments slacken, and the elastic lens becomes more convex (rounder/thicker) to refract light more strongly.

options.A: Relax and the lens becomes less convex
options.B: Contract and the suspensory ligaments slacken so the lens becomes more convex
options.C: Contract and the suspensory ligaments tighten
options.D: Relax and the suspensory ligaments slacken

subQuestions.questionText: Which hormone is NOT directly involved in regulating blood-glucose levels?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D — Oxytocin (2 marks)
Insulin, glucagon and adrenalin all directly regulate blood-glucose levels. Oxytocin is involved in childbirth (uterine contractions) and milk ejection — not blood-glucose regulation.

subQuestions.questionText:
Hormones A (insulin) and B (glucagon) are involved in blood-glucose regulation. Indicate whether each statement (1.4.1 to 1.4.5) applies to A only, B only, BOTH A and B, or NONE.

1.4.1 Lowers blood-glucose levels in the body
1.4.2 Secreted by alpha cells in the pancreatic islets
1.4.3 Released by the pancreas
1.4.4 Stimulates the conversion of glucose into glycogen in the liver
1.4.5 Causes blood-glucose level to rise
subQuestions.memoText:
Each correct answer = 2 marks (5 × 2 = 10)

1.4.2 B only ✓✓ — glucagon is secreted by alpha cells; insulin by beta cells.
1.4.3 Both A and B ✓✓ — both hormones are released by the pancreas (islets of Langerhans).
1.4.4 A only ✓✓ — insulin stimulates conversion of glucose to glycogen (glycogenesis) in the liver.
1.4.5 B only ✓✓ — glucagon causes blood-glucose level to rise (by stimulating glycogenolysis).

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why the testes are located in the scrotum, OUTSIDE the abdominal cavity.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any THREE points (3 marks):
• Spermatogenesis (sperm production) requires a temperature lower than core body temperature ✓
• The scrotum holds the testes about 2–3 °C below body temperature ✓
• The cremaster muscle contracts/relaxes to move the testes closer to or further from the body to regulate temperature ✓
• Higher (body) temperature would damage developing sperm cells, leading to infertility ✓

(any 3) [3]

X — LH (luteinising hormone) ✓

subQuestions.questionText: Which letter (W, X, Y or Z) represents the hormone that directly causes ovulation? Explain your answer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: X (LH) ✓
Mark 2: It shows a sudden / sharp surge / peak around day 14 ✓
Mark 3: This LH surge causes the mature Graafian follicle to rupture and release the secondary oocyte / ovum ✓
[3]

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the role of hormone Z in the days following ovulation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any THREE points (3 marks). Hormone Z = progesterone.
• Maintains the thickened endometrium / uterine lining ✓
• Increases the blood supply to the endometrium (preparing for implantation) ✓
• Inhibits the secretion of FSH and LH from the pituitary by negative feedback ✓
• Prevents further follicle development during the luteal phase ✓

(any 3) [3]

subQuestions.questionText: If fertilisation does NOT occur, what happens to the level of hormone Z during the last days of the cycle? Justify your answer using the graph.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: The level of hormone Z (progesterone) decreases / falls / drops ✓
Mark 2: From the graph: the Z curve drops sharply after about day 22, approaching a low value by day 28 ✓
[2]

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how the change you described in 2.2.4 leads to menstruation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: With low progesterone, the endometrium can no longer be maintained ✓
Mark 2: The endometrium / uterine lining (and its blood vessels) breaks down and is shed through the vagina as menstruation ✓
[2]

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO events that occur to the zygote as it moves down the Fallopian tube towards the uterus.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Repeated mitotic divisions / cleavage produce a ball of cells (morula → blastocyst) ✓
Mark 2: Cilia in the Fallopian tube and peristaltic muscle contractions sweep the ball of cells towards the uterus ✓
[2]

subQuestions.memoText: The placenta ✓ (1)

| Mother → Foetus | Foetus → Mother |
|---|---|
| Oxygen, glucose, amino acids, vitamins, minerals and antibodies diffuse from mother's blood to foetal blood ✓ | Carbon dioxide and urea diffuse from foetal blood to mother's blood for excretion ✓ |

Plus (endocrine function): Placenta produces hCG, oestrogen and progesterone ✓

(any 3 functions; tabulation required, otherwise lose marks) [3]

subQuestions.questionText: A pregnant woman who consumes alcohol regularly is told that the alcohol can damage her baby. Explain, with reference to the structure named in 2.3.3 (the placenta), how alcohol reaches the foetus.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Alcohol molecules are small / lipid-soluble (fat-soluble) ✓
Mark 2: They diffuse across the placental barrier from mother's blood to foetal blood ✓
Mark 3: They reach the foetus and may damage developing tissues, causing foetal alcohol syndrome (FAS) ✓
[3]

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons why mammals can afford to produce so few offspring at a time.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO points (2 marks):
• Internal fertilisation greatly increases fertilisation success ✓
• Internal development inside the uterus protects the embryo from predators and harsh conditions ✓
• Parental care and lactation provide food, warmth and protection after birth, increasing offspring survival ✓

(any 2) [2]

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why fish need to produce such a large number of eggs.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: External fertilisation is unreliable — many eggs are not fertilised ✓
Mark 2: Eggs and offspring receive no parental care, so most are eaten by predators or die from environmental factors. Producing many eggs increases the chance some will survive to adulthood ✓
[2]

subQuestions.questionText: Diabetes insipidus is caused by the kidney's inability to respond properly to ADH. Use the graph to support this statement and explain why the urine volume of Person B is so much greater than that of Person A.

subQuestions.questionText: Describe how the body of a healthy person responds when blood is too concentrated (e.g. after sweating heavily on a hot day). Refer to ADH, the kidney and urine in your answer.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Hypothalamus (osmoreceptors) detects increased osmotic pressure / decreased water in blood ✓
Mark 2: Posterior pituitary releases more ADH into the blood ✓
Mark 3: ADH increases the permeability of the distal convoluted tubules and collecting ducts to water ✓
Mark 4: More water is reabsorbed into the blood; smaller volume of more concentrated urine is produced ✓

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how the responses observed (reddening of the skin and sweating) help the body to cool down during exercise.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Reddening of skin (vasodilation): Arterioles in the skin widen, more blood flows close to the surface, more heat is lost to the surroundings by radiation/convection ✓
Mark 2: Sweating: Sweat glands release water onto the skin; the water absorbs heat as it evaporates (latent heat of vaporisation), cooling the skin ✓
Mark 3: Together these responses lower the body's core temperature back to its normal range — homeostasis ✓
[3]

Marking model. Award marks based on (i) Content marks (max 17) — for biological accuracy and detail of the points listed below — and (ii) Synthesis marks (max 3) for logical flow, comparison and use of correct scientific terminology. Award marks for any equivalent valid points. Drawings/tables may be included by candidates and are marked under content where they show the same biological idea.

=== CONTENT MARKS (max 17) ===

(a) Definitions and role of auxins (max 3):
• Auxins are plant growth hormones / chemical messengers produced in the apical meristem of shoots and root tips ✓
• Phototropism = the directional growth response of plants to light (positive in shoots, negative in roots) ✓
• Geotropism / gravitropism = the directional growth response of plants to gravity (positive in roots, negative in shoots) ✓

(b) How a SHOOT bends towards light (max 5):
• Light from one side of the shoot causes auxins to move/redistribute from the lit side to the shaded side ✓
• Auxins accumulate on the shaded (darker) side of the shoot ✓
• On the shaded side, the higher concentration of auxin causes cells to elongate more ✓
• Cells on the lit side elongate less, so the shoot bends towards the light ✓
• This is positive phototropism — increases the surface area of leaves for light absorption / photosynthesis ✓

(c) How a ROOT responds to gravity (max 4):
• In a root growing horizontally, gravity causes auxins to accumulate on the LOWER side ✓
• In roots, high concentrations of auxin inhibit cell elongation (unlike shoots) ✓
• Cells on the upper side of the root therefore elongate more than those on the lower side ✓
• This causes the root to bend downward — positive geotropism. The root anchors the plant and reaches water/minerals ✓

(d) Clinostat investigation (DIAGRAM D) (max 3):
• Setup A (stationary): gravity acts continuously in one direction. After 24 hours, all roots will have curved to grow downwards (positive geotropism) and shoots upwards (negative geotropism), regardless of the direction in which they were originally pinned ✓
• Setup B (rotating): the slow rotation continually changes the direction in which gravity acts on each seedling, so no single side receives a consistent gravitational stimulus. The seedlings continue to grow straight, along their original axis ✓
• Conclusion: Setup A is the test, Setup B is the control. The difference shows that gravity (not the rotation itself) is the cause of the geotropic response observed in Setup A ✓

(e) TWO practical applications of plant hormones in agriculture (max 2):
• Rooting hormones: dipping cuttings of stems in synthetic auxin powder / solution stimulates rapid root growth, allowing fast vegetative propagation of crops and ornamentals ✓
• Selective weed-killers (herbicides): high-concentration synthetic auxins (e.g. 2,4-D) cause rapid uncontrolled growth in broad-leaf weeds, killing them while leaving narrow-leaf cereal crops unharmed ✓
• Other accepted answers: ripening of fruit using ethylene; production of seedless fruit using auxin sprays; delaying fruit drop using gibberellins.

=== SYNTHESIS MARKS (max 3) ===

3 marks: Excellent overall coherence; logical flow from definitions → shoot response → root response → clinostat → applications; consistent use of correct scientific terminology; comparison of shoot vs root responses to auxin clearly drawn out; clinostat result explained as a controlled experiment.

2 marks: Good logical flow with most ideas linked; mostly correct terminology; one or two areas (e.g. clinostat or applications) less integrated.

1 mark: Some attempt at flow but ideas mostly listed; limited use of scientific terminology; no clear comparison or linkage between sections.

0 marks: Disjointed answer; mostly bullet points without explanation; incorrect or absent terminology.
